1986){{cite web|title=Sonny Weems NBA Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/weemsso01.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 28, 2016}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Jiaozuo Cultural Tourism]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]]. He played college basketball for the [[University of Arkansas]] and the [[University of Arkansas at Fort Smith]]. He was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]] and shortly thereafter traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He has since played for the [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the NBA, and has had stints in Lithuania and Russia. At {{height|ft=6|in=6}}, Weems plays both the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. He was an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] selection in [[2013–14 Euroleague|2014]]. ==Early life== Weems was born with [[Ectrodactyly–ectodermal dysplasia–cleft syndrome|cleft feet]], and as a child, he was told that he might not be able to walk or run. He stumbled as a youngster and endured painful childhood nights in corrective shoes before finding his stride and becoming a state long-jump and high-jump champion.{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Coro|title=Phoenix Suns' Sonny Weems took the long way back to NBA|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/07/11/phoenix-suns-sonny-weems-took-long-way-back-nba/30026185/|work=The Arizona Republic|date=July 11, 2015|access-date=February 28, 2016}}{{cite web|title=Suns One on One with Sonny Weems|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o0vwpVnEMV8|via=YouTube|date=September 16, 2015|access-date=September 16, 2015}}{{cbignore}}{{Dead Youtube links|date=February 2022}} ==High school and college career== Weems played basketball at [[West Memphis High School]] where he was named first team all-state as a senior after leading his team to the 5A state championship, and was also a 6–10 [[high jump]]er in [[track and field]]. In Weems' high school career, West Memphis posted a record of 68–10. Weems averaged over 20 points per game as sophomore and junior, and 14.0 rebounds per game as a senior. After high school, Weems attended [[junior college]] at the [[University of Arkansas-Fort Smith]], and was named 3rd team All-American, as well as all-conference and all-region as a freshman. Ranked as the number one junior college player in the nation by [[Rivals.com]] and [[Street & Smith's]], Weems took UAFS to the [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] (NJCAA) National Championship in 2006. Weems was named Honorable Mention All-American and was selected for the all-tournament team. In two seasons at UAFS, Weems led the team to a 62–7 record and back-to-back [[Bi-State Conference]] Eastern Division titles.{{cite web|title=Arkansas bio |url=http://www.hogwired.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=30749&SPID=2421&DB_OEM_ID=6100&ATCLID=648581&Q_SEASON=2007 |work=HogWired.com |access-date=October 15, 2007 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221230034/http://www.hogwired.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=30749&SPID=2421&DB_OEM_ID=6100&ATCLID=648581&Q_SEASON=2007 |archive-date=February 21, 2014 }} ===Arkansas Razorbacks=== Weems signed with the [[Arkansas Razorbacks]] as a junior, which was also [[Stan Heath]]'s final season as head coach. He averaged 11.8 points per game and was named to all-tournament teams at the [[Old Spice Classic]] and the [[SEC Tournament]] as he helped the Razorbacks to their third consecutive winning season and their second straight [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] appearance, losing to the [[USC Trojans]] in the first round. Weems played his senior season with a new head coach, [[John Pelphrey]], and was named first team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] after averaging 15.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Sonny Weems Stats, News, Photos – Arkansas Razorbacks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3467/sonny-weems |publisher=ESPN |access-date=February 13, 2014 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101224033917/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=32032 |archive-date=December 24, 2010 }} Weems led the Razorbacks to their first NCAA tournament win in nine years with an upset victory of [[Indiana University]]. He finished the game with 31 points, out-dueling the much-heralded freshman [[Eric Gordon]], who was held to only eight points.{{cite web|title=Weems' 31, Townes' double-double help Razorbacks snap 5-game tourney skid|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000048|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709065118/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000048|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 9, 2018|publisher=ESPN|date=March 22, 2008|access-date=February 13, 2014}} After his team lost in the second round of the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]], Weems later won the [[State Farm]] College [[Slam Dunk]] Championship held at the [[Final Four]].{{cite web|title=College Slam Dunk Participants – 2008|url=http://www.collegeslam.com.prod.sportngin.com/page/show/2357541-2008-participants|work=CollegeSlam.com|access-date=March 1, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===NBA=== ====NBA draft==== In April 2008, Weems accepted an invitation to participate in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], but later decided not to attend.{{cite web|first=Chris |last=Monter |url=http://collegebasketballnews.scout.com/2/744814.html |title=Ten Pull out of Portsmouth Invitational |date=April 9, 2008 |access-date=June 27, 2008 |work=Scout.com |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222220457/http://collegebasketballnews.scout.com/2/744814.html |archive-date=February 22, 2014 }} Instead, Weems worked out with several teams: the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Orlando Magic]], [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[New Jersey Nets]], [[New Orleans Hornets]], and [[Portland Trail Blazers]], receiving increased interest because of his high scores in speed and agility drills.''[[Arkansas Democrat Gazette]]'', June 26, 2008. Weems was selected with the 39th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the Bulls, but he was traded almost immediately to the [[Denver Nuggets]] for a 2009 second-round pick in a three-team trade involving the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Nuggets Acquire Draft Rights to Weems |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/weems_draft2008_062608.html |publisher=National Basketball recalled by the Denver Nuggets. ====Denver Nuggets==== Weems scored 4 points in his NBA regular season debut with the Nuggets on January 17, 2009, when he substituted for [[Anthony Carter (basketball)|Anthony Carter]] with 3:31 remaining in a 106–88 loss to [[Orlando Magic|Orlando]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic at Denver Nuggets Play-By-Play, January 17, 2009|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/pbp/200901170DEN.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|date=January 17, 2009|access-date=February 26, 2014}} On July 31, 2009, he was traded along [[Image:Sonny_Weems_Raptors.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Weems with the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2012]] On August 18, 2009, Weems was traded by the Bucks to the [[Toronto Raptors]] along with [[Amir Johnson]] in exchange for [[Carlos Delfino]] and [[Roko Ukić]].{{cite web|title=Raptors Acquire Johnson And Weems From Milwaukee|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/johnson_weems_trade081809.html|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 18, 2009|access-date=August 18, 2009}} On April 7, 2010, Weems was placed in the starting lineup and scored a then career-high 21 points to lead the Raptors, but the Raptors lost the game to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He went on to score a career-high 25 points on November 17, 2010, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. ===Europe=== ====Žalgiris Kaunas (2011–2012)==== On July 8, 2011, Weems signed a one-year contract with the Lithuanian team [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]].{{cite news|title=ZALGIRIS tabs high-flying Weems |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/86553/5611/zalgiris-tabs-high-flying-weems |access-date=February 13, 2014 |work=Euroleague.net |date=July 8, 2011 |archive-date=February 22, 2014 }}{{cite news|title=Raptors' Weems heading overseas, signs deal in Lithuania|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/07/08/weems-lithuania.ap/index.html|access-date=February officially leaves Zalgiris|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/basketball.aspx?NewsID=266654|access-date=April 4, 2012|work=Eurobasket.com|date=April 4, 2012}} Weems later complained on social media saying that he had to go to U.S. to heal his sore ankle, after not receiving any medical care in Lithuania.{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Freeman|title=Sonny Weems can't get his ankle treated in Lithuania, shows us his gross foot|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/sonny-weems-t-ankle-treated-lithuania-shows-us-222314526.html|access-date=June 17, 2015|publisher=Yahoo!|date=March 26, 2012}} Over 15 games in the [[EuroLeague]], he averaged 15.5 points and 5 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=WEEMS, SONNY|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=003443&seasoncode=E2011|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=August 21, 2012}} ====CSKA Moscow (2012–2015)==== ===== 2012–13 season ===== On July 30, 2012, he signed a three-year contract with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].{{cite news|title=Sonny Weems signed with CSKA|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=11546&lang=en|access-date=February 13, 2014|work=CSKABasket.com|date=July 30, 2012}}{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=McIntyre|title=Where are They Now: Sonny Weems Edition|url=http://www.sportsmedia101.com/torontoraptors/2013/10/18/where-are-they-now-sonny-weems-edition/|access-date=February 26, 2014|work=SportsMedia101.com|date=October 18, 2013}} His signing was largely seen as a replacement to former team leader [[Andrei Kirilenko]].{{cite news|first=Wendell|last=Maxey|title=With CSKA Moscow, Weems Has Unfinished Business in the Euroleague in Replacing Kirilenko|url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2012/8/1/3207086/with-cska-moscow-weems-has-unfinished-business-in-the-euroleague-in?_ga=1.147057266.430358256.1434527564|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=RidiculousUpside.com|date=August 1, 2012}} On October 18, 2012, he had a [[EuroLeague]] career-high 30 points in a 76–71 [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] win over [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]].{{cite news|title=CSKA survives overtime thriller at Partizan|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=23&seasoncode=E2012#!report|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=October 18, 2012}} In his first season with the team, in a roster loaded with big European names like [[Miloš Teodosić]], [[Nenad Krstić]], [[Theo Papaloukas]] and [[Victor Khryapa]], CSKA Moscow won 3rd place in the [[2013 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Four]], after a 69–52 loss to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] in the semi-final game.{{cite news|title=Olympiacos trounces CSKA, eyes repeat!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2012#!report|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=May 10, 2013}} Weems was seen as one of the team leaders, a starting small forward who averaged 13.7 points, 2.9 rebounds and 2.1 assists over 28 games in the EuroLeague. CSKA eventually won the [[2012–13 VTB United League|VTB United League]] after defeating [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]], 3–1, in the final series. ===== 2013–14 season ===== In the 2013–14 season, CSKA's roster didn't change much, and Weems was again one of the team leaders. On January 17, 2014, he had career-high 10 assists, along with 16 points, in 72–73 EuroLeague loss to Partizan Belgrade.{{cite news|title=Partizan stops CSKA in Coach Vujosevic's return to sidelines|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=143&seasoncode=E2013#!report|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=January 17, 2014}} In May 2014, Weems was named the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] of the [[2013-14 Euroleague|EuroLeague]], for his performances over the season.{{cite web|title=2013–14 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/136869|work=Euroleague.net|date=May 8, 2014|access-date=May 9, 2014}} Although his points per game slightly dropped to 12.2 in the EuroLeague, he improved his defensive play and generally had a bigger impact on the game itself. However, CSKA Moscow was yet again stopped in the semi-final game, this time to the eventual champion [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{cite news|title=Maccabi rallies from 15 down to stun CSKA, advance to championship game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2013#!report|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=May 16, 2014}} Later in the season, CSKA won its third consecutive [[2013–14 VTB United League|VTB United League]] championship by defeating [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]], 3–0, in the final series.{{cite news|title=CSKA crowned champions!!!|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-crowned-champions.htm|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=VTB-League.com|date=June 13, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617172025/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-crowned-champions.htm|archive-date=June 17, 2014}} On July 4, 2014, Weems extended his contract with the club until 2017.{{cite web|title=Sonny Weems stays in CSKA till 2017|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=13585&lang=en|website=CSKABasket.com|date=July 4, 2014|access-date=July 4, 2014}} ===== 2014–15 season ===== In the 2014–15 season, CSKA Moscow advanced to the [[2015 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Four]] for the fourth straight season, after eliminating [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] for the second straight season in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] series, 3–1.{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow routs Panathinaikos to claim Final Four berth|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=246&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=April 22, 2015}} However, in the semi-final game, despite being dubbed by media as an absolute favorite to advance, they once again lost to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. The final score was 70–68, after an Olympiacos comeback in fourth quarter, led by [[Vassilis Spanoulis]].{{cite news|title=Spanoulis comes through again as Olympiacos stuns CSKA|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=249&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=May 15, 2015}} CSKA Moscow then won the third place after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]], 86–80.{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=Eurolague.net|date=May 17, 2015}} Weems' third season saw a slight increase in statistics, as he averaged 13.1 points, 4 rebounds and 3.5 assists over 26 games played. CSKA Moscow finished the season by winning the [[2014–15 VTB United League|VTB United League]], after eliminating [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] with 3–0 in the final series.{{cite news|title=CSKA wins championship!|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-wins-championship.htm|access-date=June 10, 2015|work=VTB-League.com|date=June 8, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610135415/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-wins-championship.htm|archive-date=June 10, 2015}} On June 16, 2015, he parted ways with CSKA Moscow to return to the NBA.{{cite news|title=Thank you, Sonny!|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=14395&lang=en|access-date=June 17, 2015|work=CSKABasket.com|date=June 16, 2015}} Over three seasons spent with CSKA, Weems played in 166 games, averaging 12.1 points, 3.1 rebounds and 3 assists per game in the EuroLeague and the VTB United League. ===Return to the NBA=== ====Phoenix Suns (2015–2016)==== On July 17, 2015, Weems signed a two-year deal with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite news|title=Suns Sign Teletovic, Weems, Price|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-teletovic-weems-price|access-date=July 17, 2015|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 17, 2015}}{{cite news|first=Paul|last=Coro|title=Sonny Weems, Ronnie Price to join Suns as backup guards|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/07/08/phoenix-suns-contracts-sonny-weems-ronnie-price/29883879/|access-date=July 8, 2015|work=The Arizona Republic|date=July 8, 2015}} He made his debut for the Suns in the team's season opener against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on October 28, recording 3 rebounds, 2 assists and 1 steal in a 111–95 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|title=8 Dallas players reach double figures, Mavs rout Suns 111–95|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}} On January 26, 2016, he scored a season-high 12 points in a loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Smith, Covington lift suddenly decent 76ers past Phoenix|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160126/PHXPHI/gameinfo.html|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 26, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}} On March 5, 2016, he was waived by the Suns after averaging 2.5 points, 1.3 assists, 1.1 rebounds and 11.7 minutes in 36 games.{{cite web|title=Suns Waive Weems|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-waive-weems|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=March 5, 2016}} ====Philadelphia 76ers (2016)==== On March 7, 2016, Weems was claimed off waivers by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Sixers Claim Sonny Weems Off Waivers|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-claim-sonny-weems-waivers|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 7, 2016|access-date=March 7, 2016}} Weems struggled during his time with the 76ers, and after straining his right quadriceps on March 26 against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],{{cite web|title=McCollum helps Blazers escape with 108–105 win over 76ers|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/PHIPOR/gameinfo.html|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2016}} he was waived by the team the next day.{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Christian Wood To 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/philadelphia-76ers-sign-christian-wood-10-day-contract|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 27, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2016}} ===Return overseas=== ====Maccabi Tel Aviv (2016–2017)==== On June 14, 2016, Weems signed a two-year contract with Israeli club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{cite news|title=Maccabi tabs scoring forward Weems|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6yay7pfhtlhge8kq|access-date=June 14, 2016|work=Euroleague.net|date=June 14, 2016}} On January 30, 2017, Weems was released by the club after he failed to complete an anti-doping test.{{cite news|title=Maccabi releases Sonny Weems|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7kwutqyoumsrm7gg|access-date=February 1, 2017|work=EuroLeague.net|date=February 1, 2017}} ====Zhejiang Golden Bulls (2017–2018)==== In July 2017, Weems signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite news|title=Sonny Weems moves to China|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/479817/sonny-weems-moves-china/|access-date=November 8, 2017|work=Eurohoops.net|date=July 12, 2017}} Weems played 38 games for Zhejiang and averaged 31.7 points, 8 rebounds and 5.9 assists per game. ====Anadolu Efes (2018)==== On February 24, 2018, Weems signed with the Turkish team [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Anadolu Efes Istanbul signs Sonny Weems|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/265869/anadolu-efes-istanbul-signs-sonny-weems.html|access-date=February 24, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=February 24, 2018}} On March 1, 2018, Weems made his debut in a 64–77 loss to [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]], scoring 19 points, along with 6 rebounds and 2 assists.{{cite news|title=Sonny Weems returns with 19 points|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/626613/sonny-weems-returns-19-points/|access-date=March 3, 2018|work=eurohoops.net|date=March 1, 2018}} ====Guangdong Southern Tigers (2018–2022 & 2023-2024)==== On October 8, 2018, Weems signed with the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.{{cite news |title=Guangdong Southern Tigers land Sonny Weems |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/guangdong-southern-tigers-land-sonny-weems/ |newspaper=Sportando |access-date=October 11, 2018 |date=October 8, 2018}} With Guangdong, he won three consecutive CBA titles from 2019 to 2021, and was named [[CBA Finals Most Valuable Player|Finals MVP]] in [[2019–20 Chinese Basketball Association season|2020]] after averaging 34.7 points in a 2–1 series against [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]]. In January 2022, after the match between Liaoning Flying Leopards, Weems was involved in an altercation with Liaoning Flying Leopards player [[Han Dejun]], which resulted in both players being ejected from the match, with Han being fined $31,440 and suspended for seven games, while Weems was fined $22,008 and suspended for five games. As a result of the incident, Weems was subjected to racial abuse by Liaoning Flying Leopards fans who kept shouting "[[nigger]]" and "get out of China" at him, as he was exiting the Guangdong Southern Tigers team bus along with the rest of the team. The Liaoning Flying Leopards fans' behaviour towards Weems was condemned by the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] and basketball player [[Jeremy Lin]].{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/01/18/sport/sonny-weems-racism-china-spt-intl/index.html|title=US basketball player Sonny Weems racially abused by fans in China|first1=David|last1=Culver|first2=George|last2=Ramsay|newspaper=[[CNN]]|date=2022-02-19|access-date= 13 April 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.insider.com/chinese-basketball-racial-slurs-ex-nba-player-sonny-weems-2022-1|title=Chinese basketball fans yelled racial slurs at former Toronto Raptors player Sonny Weems and told him to 'get out of China'|first=Matthew|last=Loh|newspaper=[[Insider Inc.]]|date=2022-02-19|access-date= 13 April 2022}} ===Shanxi Loongs (2022–2023)=== In 2022, Weems signed a one-year deal with [[Shanxi Loongs]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.{{cite web|url=https://www.talkbasket.net/148513-sonny-weems-will-join-shanxi-loongs|title=Sonny Weems will join Shanxi Loongs|first=Erikas|last=Polockas|newspaper=Talk Basketball|date=2022-08-16|access-date=August 21, 2023}} ===Shenzhen Leopards (2024–2025)=== On October 13, 2024, Weems signed with [[Shenzhen Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web |title=Leopards ink Sonny Weems |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/895607/Leopards-ink-Sonny-Weems |website=www.asia-basket.com |access-date=14 October 2024}} ==Personal life== In May 2020, Weems donated protective masks to the town of [[West Memphis, Arkansas]] to help fight against [[Coronavirus]]. He wanted the elderly population and low-income families to have priority in the mask distribution as his grandmother works in the nursing home. The donation was made through this foundation called "Weems World."{{cite web |title=Sonny Weems makes "life-saving" donation to hometown |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1057750/sonny-weems-makes-life-saving-donation-to-hometown/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=14 October 2024 |language=en |date=9 May 2020}} In June 2024, Weems led the Athletes Abroad Summit which was aimed at equipping American athletes for success in international sports. He was joined by [[Kyle Hines]] and [[Edniesha Curry]].{{cite web |title=Sonny Weems and Kyle Hines to lead player advisory panel at Athletes Abroad Summit |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1680840/sonny-weems-and-kyle-hines-to-lead-player-advisory-panel-at-athletes-abroad-summit/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=14 October 2024 |language=en
